newsitem.title: USA: Senate rejects move to protect Nevada in nuke bill.
newsitem.headline: Senate rejects move to protect Nevada in nuke bill.

text.p: The U.S. Senate rejected a move Tuesday to protect Nevada in a bill that would make the government put an interim storage facility in the state for nuclear waste.
The vote of 59 to 39 to set aside the amendment gave a clue to how the Senate would vote on the whole radioactive waste storage bill, which the White House has threatened to veto.
Supporters of the bill need 67 votes to be able to override a veto on the legislation.

The amendment by Sen. Jeff Bingaman, D-N.M., sought to ensure that an aboveground temporary storage facility in Nevada would not automatically become a permanent nuclear waste dump if the government decided it could not ultimately bury the waste safely in Yucca Mountain.

Utilities, who opposed the amendment, want to ensure that spent nuclear fuel building up at their plants is taken away as soon as possible, because the governmment promised in 1982 to start removing their waste next year.

Under the bill by Sen. Frank Murkowski, R-Alaska, the government would have to build an interim storage facility in Nevada, near Yucca Mountain, until a permanent dump is ready, unless the president chooses and Congress approves another site.

Bingaman said the provision allowing for another site to be chosen was a "disguise" for a policy of dumping the waste in Nevada because Congress and the president would be unlikely to agree on a new site.
"We will then have a permanent aboveground repository (in Nevada) rather than a geologic repository," he said.
